## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T>0$ and a fixed size interval $[0,X]$. Let $g,\mu,\gamma:[0,X]\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded Lipschitz functions, with $g(x)\ge g_{\min}>0$. Here $g$ is size growth, $\mu$ is ordinary mortality, and $\gamma$ is the rate at which a dividing parent is removed. For each parent size $y$, let $K_y$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure of daughter sizes, supported on $[0,y]$. Assume $y\mapsto K_y(E)$ is measurable for every Borel set $E\subseteq[0,X]$, and that the number moment $k_0(y):=K_y([0,y])$ is uniformly bounded; the size moment $k_1(y):=\int_{[0,y]}x\,K_y(dx)$ is then finite. The **size-structured transport and division model** is

$$\partial_t n+\partial_x(gn)=-(\mu+\gamma)n+\int_{[0,X]}K_y(dx)n(t,y)\,dy,\qquad 0<x<X,$$

with zero incoming flux at $x=0$ and absorbing outflow $g(X)n(t,X)$ at $x=X$. The transport characteristic solves $x'(t)=g(x(t))$ as a first-order IVP in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. The weak equation is obtained by testing against $\phi\in C^1([0,X])$: transport contributes $\int_0^Xg\phi'n$, mortality and parent removal contribute $-\int_0^X(\mu+\gamma)\phi n$, division contributes $\int_0^X\int\phi(x)K_y(dx)n(t,y)\,dy$, and the upper boundary contributes $-\phi(X)g(X)n(t,X)$. The interval is fixed; moving boundaries, zero growth and discontinuous coefficients are outside this definition.

## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T>0$ and a nondegenerate fixed size interval $[0,X]$ with $X>0$. Let $g,\mu,\gamma:[0,X]\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded Lipschitz functions, with $g(x)\ge g_{\min}>0$. Here $g$ is size growth, $\mu$ is ordinary mortality, and $\gamma$ is the rate at which a dividing parent is removed. For each parent size $y$, let $K_y$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure of daughter sizes, supported on $[0,y]$. Assume $y\mapsto K_y(E)$ is measurable for every Borel set $E\subseteq[0,X]$, and that the number moment $k_0(y):=K_y([0,y])$ is uniformly bounded; the size moment $k_1(y):=\int_{[0,y]}x\,K_y(dx)$ is then finite. The **size-structured transport and division model** is

$$\partial_t n+\partial_x(gn)=-(\mu+\gamma)n+\int_{[0,X]}K_y(dx)n(t,y)\,dy,\qquad 0<x<X,$$

with zero incoming flux at $x=0$ and absorbing outflow $g(X)n(t,X)$ at $x=X$. Let $\Pi_{[0,X]}(x):=\min\{X,\max\{0,x\}\}$ and extend the growth field to $\widetilde g(x):=g(\Pi_{[0,X]}(x))$ on $\mathbb R$. This is a bounded Lipschitz vector field. By [[thm-size-structured-positivity-number-and-weighted-moment-identities]], its IVP has a unique solution on the finite time horizon; a model characteristic is this solution restricted to the interval from its initial size until its first hitting of $X$, including that hitting time when it occurs by $T$. On this restricted interval, $\widetilde g=g$. The characteristic is understood as a first-order IVP solution in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. The weak equation is obtained by testing against $\phi\in C^1([0,X])$: transport contributes $\int_0^Xg\phi'n$, mortality and parent removal contribute $-\int_0^X(\mu+\gamma)\phi n$, division contributes $\int_0^X\int\phi(x)K_y(dx)n(t,y)\,dy$, and the upper boundary contributes $-\phi(X)g(X)n(t,X)$. The interval is fixed; moving boundaries, zero growth and discontinuous coefficients are outside this definition.

## Definition

Partition $[0,X]$ into disjoint cells $C_j=[x_{j-1},x_j)$ for $j<J$ and $C_J=[x_{J-1},X]$, with widths $h_j=x_j-x_{j-1}>0$ and centers $x_j^c=(x_{j-1}+x_j)/2$. Let $M_j^k$ be the mass in cell $C_j$ and $u_j^k=M_j^k/h_j$. Set the incoming flux $F_0^k=0$, the internal and outgoing upwind fluxes $F_j^k=g(x_j)u_j^k$ for $1\le j\le J$, and $d_j=\mu(x_j^c)+\gamma(x_j^c)$.

For each parent cell $C_\ell$, form nonnegative daughter coefficients

$$A_{j\ell}=\frac{1}{h_\ell}\,Q_M\bigl(y\mapsto K_y(C_j);x_{\ell-1},x_\ell,1\bigr),$$

using [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]] on the parent-size interval. Since the one-panel midpoint rule is $Q_M(f;x_{\ell-1},x_\ell,1)=h_\ell f(x_\ell^c)$, this gives $A_{j\ell}=K_{x_\ell^c}(C_j)\ge0$. The finite-volume update is

$$M_j^{k+1}=M_j^k-\Delta t(F_j^k-F_{j-1}^k)-\Delta t\,d_jM_j^k+\Delta t\sum_{\ell=1}^JA_{j\ell}M_\ell^k.$$

The flux $F_J^k$ is absorbing outflow. The admissible variable-width CFL is $\Delta t(g(x_j)/h_j+d_j)\le1$ for every cell. If a grid, coefficient evaluation or kernel quadrature fails, the procedure returns an explicit failure status and performs no partial update.

Input a partition $0=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_J=X$ with $J\ge1$, a time step $\Delta t>0$, a nonnegative current mass vector $M^k=(M_j^k)_{j=1}^J$, and the coefficients and kernel from [[def-size-structured-transport-and-division-kernel]]. Partition $[0,X]$ into disjoint cells $C_j=[x_{j-1},x_j)$ for $j<J$ and $C_J=[x_{J-1},X]$, with widths $h_j=x_j-x_{j-1}>0$ and centers $x_j^c=(x_{j-1}+x_j)/2$. Set $u_j^k=M_j^k/h_j$, the incoming flux $F_0^k=0$, the internal and outgoing upwind fluxes $F_j^k=g(x_j)u_j^k$ for $1\le j\le J$, and $d_j=\mu(x_j^c)+\gamma(x_j^c)$.

For each parent cell $C_\ell$, form nonnegative daughter coefficients

$$A_{j\ell}=\frac{1}{h_\ell}\,Q_M\bigl(y\mapsto K_y(C_j);x_{\ell-1},x_\ell,1\bigr),$$

using [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]] on the parent-size interval. Since the one-panel midpoint rule is $Q_M(f;x_{\ell-1},x_\ell,1)=h_\ell f(x_\ell^c)$, this gives $A_{j\ell}=K_{x_\ell^c}(C_j)\ge0$. If $\Delta t(g(x_j)/h_j+d_j)>1$ for any cell, return `invalid-cfl` without an update. Otherwise the finite-volume update is

$$M_j^{k+1}=M_j^k-\Delta t(F_j^k-F_{j-1}^k)-\Delta t\,d_jM_j^k+\Delta t\sum_{\ell=1}^JA_{j\ell}M_\ell^k.$$

The flux $F_J^k$ is absorbing outflow. The admissible variable-width CFL is $\Delta t(g(x_j)/h_j+d_j)\le1$ for every cell. If a grid or any required coefficient/kernel evaluation fails, return failure without a partial update. Otherwise return $M^{k+1}$ together with the fluxes and daughter coefficients used in the step.

## Definition

Input a finite time step $\Delta t$, an age cutoff $A$, nonnegative rates $\mu,\beta$ on $[0,A]$, and a finite positive initial quadrature $(a_i,m_i^0)_{i=1}^I$ supported in $[0,A)$ for the initial age measure on that interval. One option is the composite midpoint rule on a partition of $[0,A]$: for each panel midpoint $a_i$, set $m_i^0=\Delta a\,n_0(a_i)$. A cohort at age $a_i^k$ and mass $m_i^k$ follows the exact age characteristic

$$a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+\Delta t$$

and updates its survival mass by forward Euler,

$$m_i^{k+1}=(1-\Delta t\,\mu(a_i^k))m_i^k.$$

At time $t_k$, calculate the finite cohort birth rate $B_h^k=\sum_i\beta(a_i^k)m_i^k$. Advance each existing cohort's age by $\Delta t$ and update its survival mass by the displayed Euler step. If its updated age is at least $A$, record that updated mass as discrete outflow and discard the cohort; otherwise retain it. Then insert a newborn cohort of age $0$ and mass $\Delta t B_h^k$ at time $t_{k+1}$. Require $\Delta t\|\mu\|_\infty\le1$. A failed rate evaluation returns failure. The procedure returns the finite positive measure $\nu_h^k=\sum_i m_i^k\delta_{a_i^k}$ and its birth/outflow records. The bounded-Lipschitz quadrature defect of the initial measure and the Euler survival error are separate inputs to any consistency claim.

## Definition

Input a finite horizon $T>0$, a time step $\Delta t>0$, an age cutoff $A>0$, bounded nonnegative rates $\mu,\beta$ on $[0,A]$, and a finite positive initial quadrature $(a_i,m_i^0)_{i=1}^I$ supported in $[0,A)$ for the initial age measure on that interval. Set $N=\lfloor T/\Delta t\rfloor$; the procedure returns levels at $t_k=k\Delta t$ for $0\le k\le N$, with final time $N\Delta t\le T$. One option is the composite midpoint rule on a partition of $[0,A]$: for each panel midpoint $a_i$, set $m_i^0=\Delta a\,n_0(a_i)$. A cohort at age $a_i^k$ and mass $m_i^k$ follows the exact age characteristic

$$a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+\Delta t$$

and updates its survival mass by forward Euler,

$$m_i^{k+1}=(1-\Delta t\,\mu(a_i^k))m_i^k.$$

If $\Delta t\|\mu\|_\infty>1$, return status invalid-step with no updates. Otherwise initialize the birth and outflow records as empty and set $\nu_h^0=\sum_i m_i^0\delta_{a_i^0}$. For each $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, first calculate $B_h^k=\sum_i\beta(a_i^k)m_i^k$. Advance every existing cohort by $a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+\Delta t$ and update its survival mass by $m_i^{k+1}=(1-\Delta t\mu(a_i^k))m_i^k$. If an updated age is at least $A$, record that updated mass as discrete outflow and discard the cohort; otherwise retain it. Then insert a newborn cohort of age $0$ and mass $\Delta t B_h^k$ at time $t_{k+1}$. Record $B_h^k$ and the step's outflow, and form $\nu_h^{k+1}$ from the retained cohorts and this newborn. A failed rate evaluation returns failure with no partial update. The procedure returns the finite sequence $(\nu_h^k)_{k=0}^N$ and its birth/outflow records. The bounded-Lipschitz quadrature defect of the initial measure and the Euler survival error are separate inputs to any consistency claim.

For [[alg-size-structured-finite-volume-flux-and-kernel-quadrature]], assume nonnegative initial masses, nonnegative quadrature coefficients $A_{j\ell}$, and the stated CFL. Then all $M_j^k$ remain nonnegative. Define the cell number and center-weighted size moment by $N_h^k=\sum_jM_j^k$ and $W_h^k=\sum_jx_j^cM_j^k$. With $k_{0,\ell}^h=\sum_jA_{j\ell}$ and $k_{1,\ell}^h=\sum_jx_j^cA_{j\ell}$, the exact balances are

$$N_h^{k+1}-N_h^k=\Delta t\left(-F_J^k-\sum_jd_jM_j^k+\sum_\ell k_{0,\ell}^hM_\ell^k\right),$$

$$W_h^{k+1}-W_h^k=\Delta t\left(\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}(x_{j+1}^c-x_j^c)F_j^k-x_J^cF_J^k-\sum_jx_j^cd_jM_j^k+\sum_\ell k_{1,\ell}^hM_\ell^k\right).$$

Thus a division kernel preserves the discrete size moment only when its first-moment production cancels the parent-removal term; this identity is not automatic for an arbitrary kernel.

## Statement

Let $\mu,\beta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded $C^1$ functions with bounded derivatives, let $n_0\in C^1([0,\infty))\cap L^1(0,\infty)$ be nonnegative, and fix $A>T$. Put $\widehat n_0=n_0\mathbf1_{[0,A-T)}$ and $\tau_A=\int_{A-T}^\infty n_0(a)\,da$. Choose the initial positive cohort quadrature for $\widehat n_0(a)\,da$ with support in $[0,A-T)$ and bounded-Lipschitz defect $\epsilon_0$ on test functions of norm at most $1$. For the procedure [[alg-age-cohort-characteristic-quadrature]], with $\Delta t\|\mu\|_\infty\le1$, define

$$\|\eta\|_{BL^*}:=\sup_{\|\phi\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(\phi)\le1}\left|\int\phi\,d\eta\right|$$

for a finite signed measure $\eta$. Then, for fixed $T$, there is $C_T$ independent of $\Delta t$, initial cohort count and cutoff such that

$$\max_{k\Delta t\le T}\|\nu_h^k-n(t_k,a)\,da\|_{BL^*}\le C_T(\epsilon_0+\Delta t+\tau_A).$$

The measure norm is weak and does not assert $L^1$ convergence of atomic cohorts to a density. The constant $C_T$ may depend on $T$, the stated coefficient bounds and $\|n_0\|_1$, but is independent of the time step, cutoff and number of cohorts. For midpoint initial cohorts on $[0,A-T]$ and Lipschitz $n_0$, $\epsilon_0=O_A(\Delta a)$; the omitted initial tail $\tau_A$ remains separate.

## Definition

For [[def-age-structured-renewal-transport-problem]], choose a finite cutoff $A>T$, an integer $J\ge1$, and use the uniform grid $a_j=j\Delta a$ with $\Delta a=A/J$ and cells $C_j=[a_{j-1},a_j]$. Given time step $\Delta t=T/N$, initial nonnegative cell masses $M_j^0$, and the values $\mu_j=\mu((a_{j-1}+a_j)/2)$, require the transport-plus-loss CFL

$$\lambda+\Delta t\,\mu_\infty\le1,\qquad \lambda=\Delta t/\Delta a,\quad\mu_\infty=\|\mu\|_\infty.$$

At time $t_k=k\Delta t$, put $u_j^k=M_j^k/\Delta a$. Compute $B_h^k$ with [[alg-age-structured-positive-birth-quadrature]] and set the upwind fluxes $F_0^k=B_h^k$ and $F_j^k=u_j^k$ for $1\le j\le J$. Update, for $1\le j\le J$,

$$M_j^{k+1}=M_j^k-\Delta t(F_j^k-F_{j-1}^k)-\Delta t\,\mu_jM_j^k.$$

The right flux $F_J^k$ is absorbing outflow: its mass $\Delta t F_J^k$ is recorded and discarded, with no inflow from ages above $A$. Invalid grids or a failed quadrature return explicit failure statuses. A `cap-reached` adaptive quadrature estimate may still be used for a finite step, but its status is retained and carries no accuracy claim.

## Definition

For [[def-age-structured-renewal-transport-problem]], input a finite horizon $T>0$, a cutoff $A>T$, integers $J,N\ge1$, and use the uniform grid $a_j=j\Delta a$ with $\Delta a=A/J$ and cells $C_j=[a_{j-1},a_j]$. Set $\Delta t=T/N$ and $t_k=k\Delta t$ for $0\le k\le N$. Input nonnegative initial cell masses $M_j^0$ and evaluate $\mu_j=\mu((a_{j-1}+a_j)/2)$. Require the transport-plus-loss CFL

$$\lambda+\Delta t\,\mu_\infty\le1,\qquad \lambda=\Delta t/\Delta a,\quad\mu_\infty=\|\mu\|_\infty.$$

If the CFL inequality fails, return status `invalid-cfl` without an update.

Initialize birth, quadrature-status, and outflow records as empty, and set cumulative outflow $O_h^0=0$. For each $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, put $u_j^k=M_j^k/\Delta a$, compute $B_h^k$ with [[alg-age-structured-positive-birth-quadrature]], and set the upwind fluxes $F_0^k=B_h^k$ and $F_j^k=u_j^k$ for $1\le j\le J$. Update, for $1\le j\le J$,

$$M_j^{k+1}=M_j^k-\Delta t(F_j^k-F_{j-1}^k)-\Delta t\,\mu_jM_j^k.$$

The right flux $F_J^k$ is absorbing outflow: record and discard the step mass $\Delta t F_J^k$, set $O_h^{k+1}=O_h^k+\Delta t F_J^k$, and allow no inflow from ages above $A$. Append $B_h^k$, the quadrature status, and the step outflow record, then proceed to step $k+1$. Return $(M^k)_{k=0}^N$ with the birth, quadrature-status, step-outflow, and cumulative-outflow records. An invalid grid or failed rate/quadrature evaluation returns failure with no partial current step. A `cap-reached` adaptive quadrature estimate may be used for a finite step, but its status is retained and carries no accuracy claim.

## Statement

Fix $T>0$ and a cutoff $A>T$. Let $n^A$ be the finite-age solution from [[thm-age-structured-renewal-finite-cutoff-characteristic-solution]] with initial density $n_0^A\in C^2([0,A])$ and assume $\mu,\beta\in C^2([0,A])$ are nonnegative and bounded. Assume $n^A$ extends to $C^2([0,T]\times[0,A])$. Its smoothness at the renewal corner includes $n_0^A(0)=B_A(0)$ and $-(n_0^A)'(0)-\mu(0)n_0^A(0)=B_A'(0)$; no boundary value is imposed at the absorbing outflow. Use exact initial cell masses, the one-panel midpoint rule in each cell from [[alg-age-structured-positive-birth-quadrature]], and a mesh with $\Delta t/\Delta a\in[c_-,c_+]$ for fixed $0<c_-\le c_+<\infty$, satisfying the transport-plus-loss CFL. Define

$$\epsilon_Q:=\max_{0\le k<N}\left|B_h(\overline M(t_k))-\int_0^A\beta(a)n^A(t_k,a)\,da\right|,$$

where $B_h(\overline M(t_k))$ is the birth-rate quadrature applied to the exact cell-average masses $\overline M_j(t_k)=\int_{C_j}n^A(t_k,a)\,da$. Then the cell-mass error $E_k=\sum_j|M_j^k-\int_{C_j}n^A(t_k,a)\,da|$ obeys

$$\max_{0\le k\le N}E_k\le C_T(\Delta a+\Delta t+\epsilon_Q).$$

The piecewise-constant reconstruction $u_h^k=M_j^k/\Delta a$ on cell $C_j$ and zero above $A$ satisfies the same $L^1$ error order. For the midpoint rule, $\epsilon_Q\le C_T\Delta a$ under the stated regularity, so the method is first order in age mesh and time step. If the capped adaptive rule is used instead, the estimate requires an independently established true $\epsilon_Q$; its reported indicator is not substituted for that hypothesis.
